name: fmcg_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Indian FMCG stocks (HUL, ITC, Nestle India, Britannia, Dabur, Marico, Godrej Consumer) are classic defensive plays with high intraday correlation (0.45-0.60) driven by: (1) shared consumer demand dynamics (rural/urban consumption), (2) common raw material costs (palm oil, milk, wheat), (3) 'flight to quality' — all FMCG stocks benefit on risk-off days. The unique pairs opportunity: ITC is an outlier because 80% of its revenue is cigarettes (excise duty sensitive) but it's classified as FMCG. When ITC diverges from the FMCG group due to tobacco-specific news (tax rumors, WHO guidelines), the other FMCG stocks are unaffected — but retail traders sell the whole sector. Similarly, HUL-specific moves (MNC premium, parent Unilever news) drag the group temporarily. These sentiment contagion effects revert within 15-30 minutes.
universe: HUL, ITC, Nestle India, Britannia, Dabur, Marico
stock_filter: HUL: ADV > ₹200 crore. ITC: ADV > ₹400 crore. Others: ADV > ₹20 crore

indicators.name: fmcg_group_return
indicators.formula: market_cap_weighted_mean(cum_return of HUL, ITC, Nestle, Britannia, Dabur, Marico)

indicators.name: itc_specific_flag
indicators.formula: 1 if abs(ITC_cum_return - fmcg_group_return_excl_itc) > 20 bps AND abs(fmcg_group_return_excl_itc) < 10 bps else 0

conditions: itc_specific_flag == 1 if the lagging stock is NOT ITC (ITC-specific move dragging group, other stocks shouldn't follow)
OR deviation_zscore < -2.0 for non-ITC stocks on a day with no ITC news
similar logic for identifying ITC-specific or HUL-specific drivers

exit.signal_exit: company-specific fundamental news confirms the divergence is justified

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 12 (in very low VIX, FMCG stocks barely move, no signal)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer divergent stock direction aligned with NIFTY FMCG direction
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 8 bps (Nestle and Britannia can be wider due to high price)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day (tobacco tax changes affect ITC specifically), result days
other_filters: skip if palm oil or crude prices move > 2% (affects FMCG margins differentially)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — FMCG sector homogeneity is driven by consumer staples demand dynamics which are structural. The ITC anomaly (tobacco classification in FMCG) is permanent and creates recurring opportunities.

weaknesses: FMCG stocks have low intraday volatility (0.3-0.8% daily range) — divergences of 12+ bps are relatively rare, limiting trade frequency.
Nestle India and Britannia have high absolute stock prices (>₹2000 and >₹5000) making lot sizes large and reducing position sizing granularity for ₹1L trades.
ITC's cigarette business makes it a fundamentally different stock from true FMCG peers. Using it in the group average distorts signals for other stocks.
prior_art: Pairs trading literature. In India, FMCG sector reports from HDFC Securities and ICICI Direct. Kaul & Nimalendran (1990) study low-volatility stock correlations. ITC's dual classification (tobacco + FMCG) is unique to India.
notes: Consider computing two group averages: (1) including ITC, (2) excluding ITC. When ITC diverges, use the excluding-ITC average for other stocks. When a non-ITC stock diverges, use the including-ITC average. This dual-mean approach improves signal quality.
